excerpt_i18n.en: The article revisits Simon's 1961 Heuristic Coder, presented as the first AI programming assistant. items.title: Runtape – counterfactual debugging and regression tests for AI agents
items.raw_excerpt: Runtape is a tool for AI agents that focuses on counterfactual debugging and regression testing. It lets developers replay agent runs, alter inputs or decision points to explore alternative outcomes, and turn those scenarios into regression tests that catch behavior changes after updates to prompts, models, or tools.

title_i18n.en: Runtape – counterfactual debugging and regression tests for AI agents
title_i18n.zh: Runtape – 面向AI代理的反事实调试与回归测试
title_i18n.es: Runtape – depuración contrafactual y pruebas de regresión para agentes de IA

excerpt_i18n.en: Runtape is a tool for AI agents that focuses on counterfactual debugging and regression testing. It lets developers replay agent runs, alter inputs or decision points to explore alternative outcomes, and turn those scenarios into regression tests that catch behavior changes after updates to prompts, models, or tools.
excerpt_i18n.zh: Runtape 是一款面向 AI 智能体的开发工具，主打反事实调试与回归测试。它让开发者能够重放智能体的运行轨迹，并通过改动其中的输入或决策点来观察不同分支下的结果，从而定位问题。同时，它支持将这些场景固化为回归测试，以便在提示词、模型或工具链变更后及时发现智能体行为的变化。

items.title: How do you handle hitting AI coding agent usage limits?
items.raw_excerpt: One topic I've been researching lately is the best way to handle switching to another agent when I hit a usage limit on one of them. For example, if I hit the usage limit on Codex, I would want to switch to Claude Code and vice versa. The important part is not losing the ongoing context/task(s) when switching between the tools.. I have found a few things that say they do this but none seem to have much traction. As a result, I was hoping to pick the brain of HN'ers to see how you all handle this (To head off comments regarding 'pay for a better plan for more usage' - I can't currently really afford the jump from $20 a month per agent to $100-200/m per agent)
